title: HUD proposal would redirect homeless-housing funds from permanent to transitional support
description_medium: A November 2025 Politico report said the Trump administration planned to change HUD’s Continuum of Care program, cutting support for permanent housing and shifting funds toward transitional housing with service or work requirements. The proposal put more than half of 2026 program funding at risk of redirection.
description_long: The Trump administration planned to change the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Continuum of Care program, which funds housing and services for people experiencing homelessness. Politico reported in November 2025 that the proposal would redirect more than half of the program’s 2026 funding from permanent housing toward transitional housing with service or work requirements. The report said permanent-housing support could fall from $3.3 billion to $1.1 billion, potentially putting about 170,000 people at risk. Existing grants were due to expire before new awards were finalized, raising concern that providers could lose funding while applications were processed. Forty-two Senate Democrats argued the planned changes could conflict with the McKinney-Vento Act, while more than 20 House Republicans urged caution about the timing and possible disruption to services. The proposal marked a major shift away from long-term housing support, though the report described planned changes rather than a final program outcome.

title: Trump family crypto venture sold $100 million in tokens to Aqua1-linked investor under UK investigation
description_medium: Aqua1 Foundation announced a $100 million purchase of World Liberty Financial tokens in June 2025. Reuters identified Guren “Bobby” Zhou as a co-founder of a related Aqua entity and reported that Britain’s National Crime Agency said he remained under investigation for suspected money laundering. Reuters reported no conviction and said Zhou denied wrongdoing.

The outlet identified Guren “Bobby” Zhou, a Chinese businessman who met Eric Trump in Dubai, as a co-founder of an entity connected to Aqua1. Britain’s National Crime Agency told Reuters that Zhou had been arrested on suspicion of money laundering in 2021, that the case was referred to prosecutors in 2022, and that he remained under investigation. Zhou has not been convicted in the matter; a statement from an Aqua entity said allegations were false. The report traces a token purchase to World Liberty Financial, not a direct payment of the full amount to Donald Trump or his sons. It also describes the venture’s international fundraising and the family’s business interests, while leaving the legal case unresolved.

title: Most Freedom 250 corporate sponsors did not disclose contributions, NOTUS reports
description_medium: A NOTUS review found that only three of 24 corporate sponsors of the Trump-supported Freedom 250 organization disclosed contributions on federal lobbying reports. Defense contractors Lockheed Martin, GE Aerospace and Northrop Grumman were among those that had not disclosed payments. The report described a potential lobbying-law violation, not a finding of intentional concealment.
description_long: A NOTUS review of federal lobbying reports found that only three of 24 corporate sponsors of Freedom 250 had disclosed contributions to the Trump-supported organization as required by the Lobbying Disclosure Act. Lockheed Martin, GE Aerospace and Northrop Grumman were among the sponsors whose contributions did not appear in the filings. NOTUS also reported that large donations from companies including TikTok, Oracle and ExxonMobil were not separately disclosed in certified reports. The article described the omissions as a potential violation of lobbying law; it did not establish that the companies deliberately concealed payments or that regulators had made a legal finding. The disclosures matter because lobbying reports are intended to show when companies with business before the federal government make contributions connected to political activity. The available account documents missing filings and raises a compliance concern, but it does not support the title’s claim that defense contractors “hid millions” from Congress.

corrected_wording.wording: Most Freedom 250 corporate sponsors did not disclose contributions in lobbying reports, according to NOTUS; the report calls the omissions a potential violation.

title: Federal judge permanently bars Trump’s proof-of-citizenship voting rule
description_medium: On June 24, 2026, U.S. District Judge Denise Casper in Boston permanently barred the Trump administration from implementing most of its 2025 election executive order, including a requirement that voters provide documentary proof of citizenship when registering. The ruling converted an earlier preliminary injunction into a permanent bar.
description_long: On June 24, 2026, U.S. District Judge Denise Casper in Boston permanently barred the Trump administration from implementing most of its first executive order on elections. The order included a requirement that people provide documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote. Casper’s ruling converted a preliminary injunction she had issued the previous year into a permanent bar. The case concerned whether the president could impose national voter-registration requirements without authorization from Congress. A separate federal case had already blocked the administration from adding the proof-of-citizenship requirement to the federal registration form. The ruling was a legal setback to Trump’s effort to change election rules through executive action. It did not bar every provision of the order; the associated reporting says it covered most of the order’s provisions overall. The full procedural status after the ruling is not described here.
